newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Iranian diplomats confirm trade ban against NZ.
newsitem.headline: Iranian diplomats confirm trade ban against NZ.

text.p: Iran's embassy to New Zealand on Monday confirmed that Tehran had cut off trade relations with New Zealand in the latest round of a diplomatic row sparked by a German court ruling linking Iran to terrorism.
In a statement, the embassy said Iran "...has ordered the suspension of all trade agreements with New Zealand parties until further notice".
The embassy also confirmed that it was recalling its ambassador to New Zealand, Mohammad Sazegara, to Tehran for consultation, saying he would be leaving on Tuesday.

New Zealand recalled its ambassador from Tehran on Friday as part of an international move to recall envoys temporarily in reaction to the German court vedict which ruled Iran had ordered the 1992 murders of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
The Wellington embassy described the trade ban as "... in protest to this unexpected move by the government of New Zealand to recall its ambassador from Iran".

It said New Zealand had entered into "a political show against Iran" by reacting in this way to the German court. Sazegara would seek to meet with his New Zealand counterpart Daniel Richards later this week when the latter is due back in Tehran, "with a view to normalising the relations between both countries on the basis of mutual respect", the statement added.
